newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-Broadcast companies seen strong in Q4.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Broadcast companies seen strong in Q4.

text.p: Radio broadcasting companies were expected to see benefits in the fourth quarter from the consolidations that took place in the early part of 1996, while television broadcasters were to get a boost from campaign advertising.

Still, the increase in advertising revenues for television stations was not expected to be as big as originally hoped, because the presidential campaign turned out not to be as much of a contest in the final stages, analysts said.
Spurred by the Telecommunications Act of 1996, which allowed for greater station ownership, there was considerable activity among radio broadcast companies.
The new law allows companies to own as many as eight radio stations in any one large market, up from four, and places no overall cap on total ownership nationwide.

"In many cases, there's a very significant change in the size of the company," said Smith Barney analyst William Meyers. "What we're seeing is a movement away from mom and pops toward these larger, better-capitalized stations."
Offered Smith Barney's Meyers, "It obviously will be a very solid quarter."
While growth among radio companies averaged about 6.5 percent in the first nine months of 1996, the fourth quarter will be "significantly better," Meyers said.

The television industry did not see the same amount of consolidation, but it is likely to show improved advertising revenues from the election season, making for a solid fourth quarter, analysts said.

LIN Television Corp, among the first of the television companies to report its fourth quarter earnings, said this week that it expects to post single-digit growth in advertising revenues for all of 1997 -- following a 1996 that saw advertising revenues propelled in part by political advertising and the Summer Olympics.

In LIN's fourth quarter, which was reported last week, it posted net income of $16.9 million, or $0.56 per share, on revenues of $71.47 million. In the prior year's fourth quarter, the company reported net income of $13.65 million, or $0.46 per share, on revenue of $63.9 million.
"Overall, the industry's particularly strong," Merrill Lynch analyst Jessica Reif said.
